name: Michigan Boat Launch Product V3
purpose: Measure whether the finder helps a boater choose a real, usable launch near a destination without sacrificing source integrity.

requirements: Every launch shown has a canonical source record or approved supplemental source.
No launch may be created by fuzzy matching, guessed coordinates, tourism copy, search snippets, or legacy fallback data.
Routing coordinates must be the same verified coordinates used by the map record.

Nullable DNR facilityid must not be used as a reason to discard otherwise valid authoritative records; use a stable source identifier such as facilityid when present, otherwise globalid/OBJECTID with provenance.
Reference-only, closed, or review-needed records must be handled explicitly and never silently promoted to verified open launches.
Bay City State Park Launch must never appear unless a future authoritative operator source establishes an actual launch there.
The primary input answers 'Where do you want to boat/launch?' by resolving a destination to coordinates and finding nearby launches geospatially.
Destination search must not depend on the destination text appearing in the launch name, waterbody, county, or description.
Default search radius is useful for trailered boaters and expands transparently when too few verified results exist.
Known coastal destination acceptance cases must return at least one verified result and should return a 3-5 launch shortlist when the source inventory supports it.
Launch-name search remains available as a secondary behavior.
Each result answers distance from destination, access waterbody, ramp type/class, trailer parking, lanes, fee/passport, operator, hours/closure status when available, and source freshness.
Results explain why a launch may fit a trailer boat, smaller boat, or carry-down user using only source-backed facts.
Missing data is labeled unknown/not listed rather than inferred.
The first screen produces a usable shortlist without requiring the user to understand DNR field names.
Searching a destination recenters the map on that destination and its result set.
Map pins and cards are keyed bidirectionally to the same source record.
The selected destination is visually distinct from launch pins.
The default view never presents an empty-looking map when verified launches exist nearby.
Phone and tablet layouts keep map, shortlist, filters and directions usable without excessive scrolling.
Directions opens the verified launch coordinate, not the destination center or a guessed address.
Nearest relevant NOAA/NWS marine observations may help compare launches but are labeled regional and never converted into an unsupported safety guarantee.
Closures and official hazard sources outrank convenience scoring.
The interface distinguishes facility facts from live/regional conditions.
Canonical URL, indexable explanatory copy, structured data and regional internal links remain intact.
Core destination interaction is fast on mobile and does not require loading the entire UI before showing useful status.
Analytics measure destination searches, zero-result searches, launch selections and directions clicks without storing precise user location.

fatalFailures: Any known false launch is displayed as real.
Any displayed launch lacks traceable source evidence.
A map or directions coordinate differs materially from the verified source coordinate without an explicit correction source.
A core acceptance destination returns zero launches when the verified inventory contains a launch within the configured search radius.
Destination search is implemented only as substring matching over launch-record text.
The production path can fall back to guessed, legacy, or fuzzy-matched launch coordinates.
The source API excludes valid authoritative records solely because a nullable human-facing facility ID is absent.
Source/API failure is rendered as a normal zero-result search rather than a distinct data-unavailable state.
The shortlist is ordered by straight-line distance when drive-distance routing is available.
A destination with no Great Lakes launch in range is given a distant launch instead of being told the inland inventory is out of scope.
An unlisted DNR field is treated as a zero value by a refinement.

acceptanceDestinations.note: The DNR greatlakesaccess field misclassifies the connecting rivers, so this case fails if that repair is reverted.
Must return the out-of-scope state, not a launch 72 miles away explained as a widened radius.
Second inland case so the acceptance set is not drawn only from the coastline the data covers.

releaseRule: Do not merge or deploy unless score is at least 95/100, there are zero fatal failures, source queries have been runtime-verified, and the preview has been manually exercised for Bay City/Saginaw Bay plus at least four geographically diverse acceptance destinations on phone and desktop.

rankingPolicy.orderedBy: driving distance from the searched destination
rankingPolicy.candidateFilter: straight-line distance, used only to choose which launches get measured because a road can never be shorter than the crow flies
rankingPolicy.routingOutage: fall back to straight-line order and label it as straight-line rather than presenting it as drive distance
rankingPolicy.why: Straight-line ranking put a 73 minute drive around Grand Traverse Bay above launches reachable in half the time, and ranked Bay City's slowest nearby launch first.
